papers.title_en: Risk-Controlled KV-Cache Eviction: From Memory Budgets to Risk Targets
papers.authors: Beomgu Kang, SoJin Yun, Hojoon Kim, Hyunseok Seo
papers.evidence: 将KV缓存驱逐重构为部署风险控制
papers.tldr: KV-cache驱逐常以平均质量-内存权衡评估，但平均损失小仍可能掩盖单请求效用显著下降。本文将驱逐重构为部署风险控制，以相对全KV推理的任务效用退化频率定义风险，并用压缩器无关的后验认证从校准数据选择保留策略，未认证则回退全KV。实验在Llama/Mistral与LongBench/RULER-32K上表明，同一可靠性合约可认证不同驱逐强度：Llama LongBench可认证SnapKV 75%保留，RULER-32K无压缩策略通过。该框架把部署可靠性要求转化为KV内存操作点。
papers.abstract_en: KV-cache eviction is typically evaluated through average quality-memory trade-offs, yet a small average loss can hide requests whose utility degrades materially. We reformulate eviction as a deployment risk-control problem: a material degradation occurs when eviction lowers task utility by more than a deployment-specified tolerance relative to full-KV inference on the same request, and deployment risk is the population frequency of such events. Given a reliability contract specifying a target risk level and confidence requirement, we use a compressor-agnostic post-hoc certification procedure to select a retention policy from calibration data with a finite-sample guarantee, falling back to full KV when no compressed policy is certified. Across multiple eviction methods, Llama and Mistral models, and LongBench and RULER-32K, the same contract supports substantially different levels of eviction: on Llama, it certifies SnapKV at 75% retention on LongBench but no tested compressed policy on RULER-32K, triggering full-KV fallback. Policies with empirical degradation rates below the 5% target can still fail finite-sample certification; on Llama LongBench, empirical thresholding selects uncertified policies that retain 5-10 percentage points less cache across fixed-budget methods. The proposed framework converts a deployment-level reliability requirement into a KV-memory operating point.

papers.title_en: ARM: Attention with Routed-Memory for Learnable Sparse Control
papers.authors: Qiuhao Zeng, Jerry Huang, Peng Lu, Ruiyi Fang, Gezheng Xu, Zihao Jing, Yufei Cui, Charles Ling, Gang Niu, Boyu Wang
papers.evidence: 可微分KV缓存结构避免硬驱逐
papers.tldr: 长上下文推理中，LLM 受限于 KV 缓存增长；选择性 token 驱逐与剪枝虽缓解压力，却易丢弃关键信息。ARM 提出可微、固定大小的路由记忆结构，用 Gumbel-Softmax 选择记忆槽，并通过 sigmoid 门控软更新新旧信息，避免硬驱逐。它还训练策略在推理时动态决定访问记忆量，以适配简单上下文与深层推理。在常识和长上下文推理基准上，ARM 相比固定 KV 缓存取得更优性能与效率，兼顾内存和生成延迟。
papers.abstract_en: Despite advances in long-context inference, large language models (LLMs) remain fundamentally limited by the key-value (KV) caching mechanisms that are necessary for stable computation. Techniques such as selective token eviction and pruning have vastly mitigated these issues, but often discard core information to manage the growing cache. In this paper, we propose Attention with Routed Memory (ARM) a novel KV caching structure that introduces a fully differentiable, fixed-size memory system organized as a hierarchical router. Via a Gumbel-Softmax, ARM learns to select memory slots and perform sigmoid-gated updates that softly combine new and stored information, avoiding hard eviction and reducing information loss. By further training a policy to dynamically select varying amounts of memory at inference, ARM adapts its accesses for both simple contexts and inputs that require deeper reasoning, enabling more scalable and effective retrieval on both short- and long-contexts. Experimental results on standard commonsense and long-context reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that ARM achieves superior performance and efficiency compared to fixed KV-caching approaches, while remaining efficient and scalable in terms of both memory and generation latency.

papers.title_en: PrefixBench-H100: Characterizing Prefix Reuse and Time-to-First-Token in H100 LLM Serving
papers.authors: Omkar Shewale, Deepak Kumar, Divakar Kumar Yadav
papers.evidence: 刻画LLM服务中前缀KV缓存复用与首token时延的基准，覆盖智能体框架场景
papers.tldr: 重复提示前缀在系统提示、RAG与多轮对话中常见，vLLM和TensorRT-LLM虽支持KV缓存复用，但在H100上何时真正提速仍不清晰。本文提出PrefixBench-H100，在单张H100上以合成、聊天和检索式负载评测两种运行时，并改变前缀长度、后缀多样性、并发和输出长度。结果显示，前缀复用可在特定区间大幅降低首token延迟，但缓存压力会侵蚀收益；缓存有效性对并发和输出长度不敏感，跨运行时差异主要来自调度层，给出H100级复用边界。
papers.abstract_en: Repeated prompt prefixes are increasingly common in LLM serving workloads, appearing in system prompts, templated retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, agent frameworks, and multi-turn conversations. Modern inference runtimes such as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM provide mechanisms for reusing previously computed KV-cache state across requests, yet it remains unclear when prefix reuse materially improves serving performance on contemporary accelerators and when its benefits are limited by scheduling, cache granularity, concurrency, or memory pressure.   This paper presents PrefixBench-H100, a reproducible benchmark and measurement framework for characterizing prefix reuse on a single NVIDIA H100. PrefixBench-H100 combines controlled synthetic traces with chat-style and retrieval-style workloads, and evaluates two widely used LLM serving runtimes under matched workload conditions. The benchmark varies shared-prefix length, suffix diversity, request arrival pattern, concurrency, output length, and cache configuration, while collecting time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, end-to-end latency, throughput, cache-hit statistics, GPU memory usage, and selected profiling traces.   The goal of PrefixBench-H100 is not to introduce a new caching algorithm, but to expose the practical operating envelope of prefix reuse for H100-class LLM serving. The study identifies the regime where prefix reuse provides substantial first-token latency reductions and the regime where cache pressure erodes them, while showing that cache effectiveness itself is largely insensitive to concurrency and output length; the cross-runtime differences that remain arise above the cache, in the scheduling layer.
